Exactly. We don’t take these drugs to hallucinate. It’s a nice sensual high, when you know how to use them and are familiar w then I’ve become incredibly comfortable with them... taken them countless times, datura, belladonna, mandrake, brugmansia, henbane. I’ve yet to die, I’ve yet to go nutso, I’ve yet to have blurry vision. I’ve had no adverse effects because I respect and know the medicine.

That’s why you don’t trip on them and you get a much milder and safer high out of them. I’ve researched and learned off of professionals and these plants have a spot for recreation, medicine and spiritual use alongside all my other plants with no two thoughts about it.

Look up Sarah Lawless. She’s the most popular of MANY online nightshade vendors. Sold in oils and ointments and in rarer cases, tinctures, for very experienced practitioners. None of the fellow users I know hallucinate on these plants or have any desire to. Hallucination is overdose threshold. Otherwise learning how to take this plant is just the same as any other herb or drug- by the drop, little by little. Most would expect to buy Sarah’s ointment and have horrible trip but you could lather yourself in her ointments and just get a very nice high. (Though obviously don’t “lather” yourself in these substances, find where and how much works best for you in small, slowly increasing amounts). 
That said, it still is poison. But in small-moderate, irregular & infrequent doses it’s really no more harmful to you than an ibuprofen. & just like ibuprofen, it should not become a habit. This is an old time pain killer we’re talking about here, and an accumulative poison none the less. That small smudgin of belladonna on your wrist isn’t going to make you trip unless you use it EXCESSIVELY, nor will the plants do you any real harm unless this is done. 
This is a drug that has much danger but when you understand after some testing how it works on your body it can become just as safe as lavender ;)

Yes she is a witch but shes a very experienced, professional herbalist. She makes her living and feeds her family selling those ointments. Her herbal career evolved into nightshade products only. She’s Canadian, these plants aren’t FDA approved and have half decent research but we have many many many users here with years of experience who can vouch for its safety and power as a medicine. These plants have been being used for forever and the only people who have anything bad to say about it are those who were stupid and didn’t respect the plant or their own bodies & safety.
But yes, unfortunately, we don’t truly know long term what taking these medicines will do to your organs and your brain. But having seen practitioners with decades of use with nothing bad to report when using the medicines correctly convinces they’re pretty alright to take. And no, it’s not comparable to saying it’s okay to take a little bit of rat poison to get high. Much more comparable to alcohol, another poison that can bring joy and sedation in proper, respectable doses and death in others.

Toad is an animal very closely associated with if not the front runner for the European witches animal. They were revered for their ugliness, their poisonousness, and their liminal nature as creatures who lived on the land, in the water, and in the soil during their hibernation. Back in the day, you’d see a lot more “earth sea and sky” three realms concept, and the toad lives in all 3. They were seen as very otherworldly, chthonic and powerful creatures, either of the faery folk or demonic, or the accomplices witches, or both. The Devil often came to witches in the guise of a toad, and the witches who had toad familiars were seen as exceptional and powerful witches, as were their familiars, who they may have dressed in silk and bells and treated specially.

I am! :) not Satan, but “the Devil” entirely nonetheless. I practice traditional witchcraft and I believe the actual spirit of the witches Devil, horns, hooves and all, is another spirit separate from and predating the concept of Satan who was called Satan or the Devil because of his profane nature.

Spirits that aren’t the human dead tend to have different morals than us, the fey are especially complex and tricky creatures. Their social and ethical standards are very different from ours. When thanked, they’re offended, as to them it implies they’re “subservient”, as if you had some authority in the matter of their decision of helping you out, or in any situation, however they treat you. 
It’s a weird stubborn relationship where yes, negotiating can be done but they will always have it their way. And their way... it’s very often difficult to fully read or understand what they’re feeling/doing and why, there’s more strings attached than meets the eye to the interactions between you two, and they have many hidden social etiquettes to work around to avoid any disrespect that might inspire mischief or harm; and even then, even just meeting them may be enough for them to decide to mess with you. They’re a rowdy bunch and it requires a lot of cunning and creativity to be able to work with them and come out both unscathed or mislead.
